reconcile.note: Adam Clarke reads 'son of Nahor' as a Hebrew idiom for grandson, since Laban was literally the son of Bethuel, who was himself the son of Nahor.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells catalogues the two verses as flatly conflicting answers to who fathered Laban, Bethuel in one and Nahor in the other, without treating 'son' as an idiom for grandson.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells (2013), Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Who was Laban's father?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/laban.html).

sides.snippet: Laban, son of Bethuel the Syrian, Rebekah's brother, Jacob's and Esau's mother.
sides.verseText: Isaac sent Jacob away. He went to Paddan Aram to Laban, son of Bethuel the Syrian, Rebekah's brother, Jacob's and Esau's mother.

sides.snippet: Do you know Laban, the son of Nahor?
sides.verseText: He said to them, \"Do you know Laban, the son of Nahor?\" They said, \"We know him.\"
